parsed.answer: The evidence directly links specificity determinants of the CheA(3)-CheY(6) interaction to phosphotransfer efficiency: a cognate methionine finger plus adjacent alanine was required for binding, and introducing these residues into noncognate CheYs dramatically changed their specificity, enabling protein interaction and rapid phosphotransfer from CheA(3)-P. Mutagenesis of the methionine and two adjacent residues abolished both binding and phosphotransfer. Thus, rapid phosphotransfer is correlated with (governed by the same determinants as) histidine kinase regulator specificity.
